title: A Day Without Electricity
description: A family spends a whole day without power after a storm.
instructions: Read the text about a day without electricity, then choose the best answer (A, B, C or D) for each question.

paragraphs.text: Last winter, there was a big storm in our town. In the morning, the electricity stopped working in every house on our street. We could not use the lights, the TV or the computer. My brother Sam and I could not charge our phones either.
At first, Sam was very unhappy. 'What can we do all day?' he asked. My mother found some old board games in a box under the bed. We sat at the kitchen table and played for hours.

We could not use the electric cooker, so my father made a fire in the garden. We cooked sausages and potatoes on it for lunch. It was cold outside, but the food tasted wonderful. Our neighbour, Mrs Green, came and ate with us.

In the evening, we lit candles and my grandfather told us stories about his childhood. The electricity came back at ten o'clock at night. Sam looked at his phone, then put it down again. 'That was a good day,' he said quietly.

The next morning, the electricity was working and the house was warm again. But at breakfast, Sam asked a strange question. Usually he loved his phone more than anything, so we were very surprised. 'Can we have a day with no electricity every month?' My parents looked at each other and laughed. Then my father said, 'Why not? Let's try it on the first Sunday of every month.'

So now we have our 'dark Sunday' once a month. We turn off the TV, the computers and our phones. We play games, read books and go for long walks in the park. In the evening, we all cook dinner together, and everyone helps. Sometimes we invite Mrs Green for lunch, and she brings a big apple pie. She says our family is quieter and friendlier than before.

Of course, it is not always easy. Last month it was very hot, and we really wanted to use the fan, but we went swimming in the river instead. My grandfather now knows more games than anyone, and he is teaching us to play chess. I think our dark Sundays are better than a normal weekend. Sam agrees, but he still checks his phone at ten o'clock at night!
